The '''2015–16 Primeira Liga''' (also known as '''Liga NOS''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 82nd season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. The fixtures were determined by draw on 4 July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Calendário Liga NOS 2015–2016|trans-title=Liga NOS 2015–2016 Calendar|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/65966/Calendario-Liga-NOS-2015-2016.pdf|publisher=LPFP|access-date=16 August 2015|language=pt|format=PDF|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913110051/http://www.ligaportugal.pt/media/65966/Calendario-Liga-NOS-2015-2016.pdf|archive-date=13 September 2015|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The season began on 14 August 2015 and concluded on 15 May 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Época 2015-2016 começa em Aveiro, com o CD Tondela-Sporting CP|trans-title=2015–2016 season begins in Aveiro, with CD Tondela vs. Sporting CP|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/noticias/arranque-da-liga-nos/|publisher=LPFP|date=13 August 2015|access-date=16 August 2015|language=pt}}</ref>

[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] won their third consecutive and 35th overall title, after beating [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] 4–1 in their last match. They finished the league with a record 88 points in 34 matches (from 29 wins and one draw), two points more than runners-up [[Sporting CP]].<ref name="LPFP last day">{{cite news|title=Liga NOS, última jornada: SL Benfica vence CD Nacional (4–1) e conquista o "tri" campeonato|trans-title=Liga NOS, last matchday: SL Benfica beat CD Nacional (4–1) and win a third consecutive championship title|url=http://www.ligaportugal.pt/noticias/liga-nos,-ultima-jornada-sl-benfica-vence-cd-nacional-(4-1)-e-conquista-o-tri-campeonato/|access-date=16 May 2016|publisher=LPFP|date=15 May 2016|language=pt}}</ref>

[[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]] and [[C.F. União|União da Madeira]] entered the season as the two promoted teams from the [[2014–15 Segunda Liga]]. On the last matchday, both teams were at risk of returning to the second division, but the combination of their results dictated União da Madeira's relegation alongside [[Associação Académica de Coimbra – O.A.F.|Académica]].<ref name="LPFP last day"/>

==Teams==
For the second consecutive season, the league was contested by a total of 18 teams, which included the best 16 sides from the [[2014–15 Primeira Liga|2014–15 season]] and two promoted from the [[2014–15 Segunda Liga]].

[[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]] made their debut in the top flight of Portuguese football, after winning the 2014–15 Segunda Liga title. while runners-up [[C.F. União|União da Madeira]] returned for the first time since the [[1994–95 Primeira Divisão|1994–95 season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Tondela campeão; União carimba subida|trans-title=Tondela champions; União seal promotion|url=http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=550829|publisher=[[A Bola]]|date=24 May 2015|access-date=16 August 2015|language=pt|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150720001258/http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=550829|archive-date=20 July 2015|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> These two clubs replaced [[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]], relegated after four seasons in the Primeira Liga, and [[F.C. Penafiel|Penafiel]], who returned to the second division one season after being promoted.

For the first time since the [[1990–91 Primeira Divisão|1990–91 season]], the autonomous region of [[Madeira]] was again represented at the highest level of Portuguese football with three teams: União da Madeira, [[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]] and [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]], all set in [[Funchal]] making the ''madeirense'' capital the second town having three teams in Primeira Liga after Lisbon.

===Match streaks===
{{updated|15 May 2016}}{{citation needed|date=January 2026}}

*Longest winning run: '''12 matches'''
**[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], from matchday 23 (20 February 2016) to matchday 34 (15 May 2016)
*Longest unbeaten run: '''14 matches'''
**[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], from matchday 9 (30 October 2015) to matchday 21 (5 February 2016)<!--(including postponed matchday 7 match against União da Madeira)-->
**[[FC Porto|Porto]], from matchday 1 (15 August 2015) to matchday 14 (20 December 2015)
*Longest winless run: '''15 matches'''
**[[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]], from matchday 20 (31 January 2016) to matchday 34 (14 May 2016)
*Longest losing run: '''6 matches'''
**[[Associação Académica de Coimbra – O.A.F.|Académica]], from matchday 1 (17 August 2015) to matchday 6 (28 September 2015)
**[[C.D. Tondela|Tondela]], from matchday 9 (30 October 2015) to matchday 14 (20 December 2015)
*Most consecutive draws: '''5 matches'''
**[[F.C. Arouca|Arouca]], from matchday 5 (20 September 2015) to matchday 9 (1 November 2015)
